The piano had been silent for three years. It stood in the corner of the parlor like a monument to something no one would name, its black surface gathering a fine democracy of dust. She lifted the lid one afternoon in December, and the keys looked up at her like teeth in a smile she had almost forgotten. She pressed middle C. The note rose, imperfect and slightly flat, wobbling through the air like a bird testing a wing it did not trust. Then she played a chord. Then a phrase. Then a melody that had lived inside her fingers all along, patient as seeds beneath frozen ground... waiting, simply waiting, for the thaw. The room filled with sound the way a jar fills with light. Not all at once. Gradually. Until every corner was luminous with it. Her daughter stood in the doorway, listening. She had never heard her mother play. She thought it sounded like someone remembering how to breathe.
